# Input Data & Configuration

## Libraries
```{r libs, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE, results = "show", warning = FALSE, error = TRUE, message = FALSE}
date()
rm(list=ls())
library(tidyverse)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(leaflet)
library(htmltools)
library(htmlwidgets)
library(plotly)
Sys.setenv(LANG = "en-US.UTF-8")
```


## Load TOPS data
```{r loadTOPS, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE, results = "show", warning = FALSE, error = TRUE, message = FALSE}
load(file = "data/TOPS/TOPS_data.Rda")
load(file = "data/TOPS/vuln_roles.Rda")
load(file = "data/TOPS/retrieve_date.Rda")
load(file = "data/TOPS/injury_severity.Rda")
injury_severity_pal <- colorFactor(palette = injury_severity$color, levels = injury_severity$InjSevName)

```

## Summarize data by county
```{r summarizeData, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE, results = "show", warning = FALSE, error = TRUE, message = FALSE}

county_summaries <- TOPS_data %>%
  group_by(CNTYNAME, year, ped_inj_name) %>%
  summarize(count = n())

```

## Make graphs
```{r makeGraphs, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE, results = "show", warning = FALSE, error = TRUE, message = FALSE}

#county_focus <- "MILWAUKEE"
county_focus <- unique(county_summaries %>% pull(CNTYNAME))

injury_focus <- c("Suspected Serious Injury", "Fatality")

wisconsin_crash_summary <- ggplotly(
ggplot(data = county_summaries %>% 
         filter(CNTYNAME %in% county_focus) %>% 
         filter(ped_inj_name %in% injury_focus) %>%
         group_by(year, ped_inj_name) %>%
         summarize(count = n()) %>%
         mutate(Year = year, "Injury severity" = ped_inj_name, "Number of crashes" = count)) +
  geom_col(aes(x = Year,
               y = `Number of crashes`,
               fill = `Injury severity`)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = injury_severity_pal(injury_severity %>% filter(InjSevName %in% injury_focus) %>% pull(InjSevName))) +
  labs(title = "People walking and biking injured in car crashes in Wisconsin")
)

dynamic_crash_summary_dir <- "figures/dynamic_crash_summaries/"
if(!dir.exists(dynamic_crash_summary_dir)){dir.create(dynamic_crash_summary_dir)}
saveWidget(wisconsin_crash_summary, 
           file = paste0(dynamic_crash_summary_dir,"wisconsin_crash_summary.html"), 
           selfcontained = TRUE,
           title = "Wisconsin Crash Summary")
```

```{r makeGraphsDropdown, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE, results = "show", warning = FALSE, error = TRUE, message = FALSE}
# 1. Prepare Data: Combine "All of Wisconsin" with individual counties
all_wi <- county_summaries |> 
  filter(ped_inj_name %in% injury_focus) |> 
  group_by(year, ped_inj_name) |> 
  summarize(count = n(), .groups = "drop") |> 
  mutate(CNTYNAME = "All of Wisconsin")
  
plot_data <- county_summaries |> 
  filter(ped_inj_name %in% injury_focus) |> 
  mutate(CNTYNAME = paste0(str_to_title(CNTYNAME), " County")) |> 
  bind_rows(all_wi) |> 
  mutate(Year = year, `Injury severity` = ped_inj_name, `Number of crashes` = count) |> 
  ungroup()
  
# 2. Ensure uniform data structure (so every county has the exact same number of traces)
plot_data_complete <- plot_data %>%
  tidyr::complete(CNTYNAME, Year, `Injury severity` = injury_focus, fill = list(`Number of crashes` = 0))
  
# 3. Setup lists and fetch correct palette colors
county_list <- c("All of Wisconsin", sort(setdiff(unique(plot_data_complete$CNTYNAME), "All of Wisconsin")))
severity_colors <- injury_severity_pal(injury_focus)
names(severity_colors) <- injury_focus

# 4. Build the base Plotly graph
p <- plot_ly()

for (county in county_list) {
  c_data <- plot_data_complete %>% filter(CNTYNAME == county)
  
  for (severity in rev(injury_focus)) {
    sev_data <- c_data %>% filter(`Injury severity` == severity)
    
    # Add a trace for every combination. 
    p <- p %>% add_bars(
      x = sev_data$Year,
      y = sev_data$`Number of crashes`,
      name = severity,
      legendgroup = severity,
      marker = list(color = severity_colors[[severity]]),
      showlegend = (county == "All of Wisconsin"),
      visible = (county == "All of Wisconsin"),
      hovertemplate = paste0(severity, ": %{y}<extra></extra>") 
    )
  }
}

# 5. Create the native Plotly dropdown visibility logic
dropdown_buttons <- lapply(seq_along(county_list), function(i) {
  
  # Create a vector of FALSE for all traces in the graph
  visibility_vector <- rep(FALSE, length(county_list) * length(injury_focus))
  
  # Turn TRUE only for the traces belonging to the currently selected county
  start_idx <- (i - 1) * length(injury_focus) + 1
  end_idx <- i * length(injury_focus)
  visibility_vector[start_idx:end_idx] <- TRUE
  
  list(
    method = "update",
    args = list(
      list(visible = visibility_vector), # Toggles the bars
      list(title = paste("People walking and biking injured in car crashes in", county_list[i]))
    ),
    label = county_list[i]
  )
})

# 6. Apply dropdown to the layout
p <- p %>% layout(
  title = "People walking and biking injured in car crashes in All of Wisconsin",
  barmode = "stack",
  xaxis = list(title = "Year", tickformat = "d"),
  yaxis = list(title = "Number of crashes"),
  updatemenus = list(
    list(
      active = 0,
      y = 1.15,
      x = 0.0,
      buttons = dropdown_buttons
    )
  )
)

# 7. Save natively as a standalone widget! No hacks required.
saveWidget(
  p, 
  file = "figures/dynamic_crash_summaries/county_crash_summaries.html", 
  selfcontained = TRUE,
  title = "County Crash Summaries"
)

browseURL("figures/dynamic_crash_summaries/county_crash_summaries.html")
```
